Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: Evidence sufficient to quantify the share of government payments digitized (to map into <20%, 20–49%, 50–69%, 70–89%, >89%) was not found in sources reviewed. Sources mention progress digitizing salaries/aid/tax collection, but not an overall percentage of government payment flows digitized.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Full-path check found this row was mislabelled as having no relevant evidence: an authoritative government source (AIP news agency, 22 May 2024) reports Presidential Decree No. 2024-272 (8 May 2024) generalising the Treasury's TrésorPay-TrésorMoney platform as the exclusive digital tool for non-tax revenue collection and mass expenditure payment across all public administrations, with the Finance Minister citing a deployment rate of 55% in 2023 rising to a target of at least 90% in 2024. A 2021 World Bank FISF technical note shows government payment digitisation in Côte d'Ivoire was still at an early "as-is" mapping stage circa 2019-2020, and UNSGSA materials (2021-2022) cite a government ambition (not a measured outcome) to digitise 80% of financial flows by 2024. The 55%/90% figures most plausibly describe administrative deployment/coverage of the TrésorPay-TrésorMoney platform rather than the percentage of total government payment value or volume routed through it, and no source separately quantifies the latter. Given this ambiguity between platform coverage and payment-value share, and per the rule against upgrading on a single source of unclear scope, this is flagged for human review rather than assigned a firm code; a plausible range is 3 (50-69%) for 2023 rising toward 4-5 for 2024 if the decree's target is verified as achieved and interpreted as payment-value share.
revised_comments: Côte d'Ivoire's Treasury has, by Presidential Decree No. 2024-272 (8 May 2024), mandated exclusive use of its TrésorPay-TrésorMoney digital platform for non-tax revenue collection and mass public expenditure payments across all public administrations and parapublic bodies. The Ministry of Finance and Budget reported the platform's deployment rate reaching 55% of relevant public services in 2023, with a target of at least 90% in 2024. TrésorPay-TrésorMoney also processes salary payments, student financial aid, tax collection and, since 2024, traffic fines, and offers a public e-wallet (TrésorMoney) accessible via app or USSD (*760#) with over 6,000 distribution points nationwide. The overall proportion of total government payment value or volume specifically digitised, as opposed to the share of administrations onboarded to the platform, is not separately reported in available sources.

revision_notes: Full-path check found this row was mislabelled as having no relevant evidence. The UNHCR/UNICEF Gulf of Guinea Joint Response Plan 2024 - Côte d'Ivoire Report (fetched and read) documents that 33,881 asylum-seekers (a 142% increase on 2023) received unconditional monthly cash transfers in 2024, coordinated with the national refugee agency DAARA, and that enrolment of asylum-seekers in the National Register of Physical Persons (RNPP) via ONECI (the national civil status/identification office) was approved for implementation in 2025, with a biometric data-transfer plan being validated to enable issuance of a unique identifier. However, the same report explicitly states that "financial inclusion is estimated to remain marginal" because of difficulties accessing certain financial services without a unique identifier. This is treated as Partial access (code 2): a documented pathway and humanitarian cash-transfer programme exist, but general legal/practical access to mainstream digital payment accounts remains constrained pending the identifier rollout. Score raised from 0 to 2 on this authoritative, directly relevant source.
revised_comments: Refugees and asylum-seekers in Côte d'Ivoire have partial access to digital/cash payment mechanisms. In 2024, 33,881 asylum-seekers received unconditional monthly cash transfers coordinated with the national refugee agency DAARA (Direction d'Aide et d'Assistance aux Réfugiés et Apatrides), a 142% increase on 2023. Enrolment of asylum-seekers in the National Register of Physical Persons (RNPP), managed by the national civil status and identification office ONECI, was approved for roll-out from 2025, with a biometric data-transfer plan being finalised to allow issuance of a unique identifier that would facilitate access to national financial and other services. Despite these pathways, broader financial inclusion for this population is assessed as remaining marginal, constrained by the current absence of a recognised unique identifier needed to open mainstream digital payment accounts.
